description: 4 should-trigger + 4 should-not-trigger. Should-trigger covers writing a commit message, placing a ticket id per git.commit_format, reviewing a subject, and a German phrasing. Should-not-trigger covers near-miss neighbours (git workflow / PR creation, rewriting already-pushed history, branch naming for a worktree) plus one unrelated counterexample.

queries.q: write a commit message for these staged changes
where does the ticket id go: DEV-1234 feat(api): ... or feat(DEV-1234): ...?
is 'fix: changes' a good commit subject?
schreib mir eine Commit-Nachricht mit Ticketnummer vorne
push this branch and open a pull request
queries.note: PR creation and the push flow belong to git-workflow, not to message writing

queries.q: squash my last three pushed commits into one
queries.note: rewriting published history is git-history-discipline's territory

queries.q: create a worktree for the export ticket
queries.note: branch and worktree creation is /worktree:create, not commit-message authoring

queries.q: how do I paginate a REST endpoint?
